Built the FETCH and PRICE half of "Four actions, three prices" in the copy /home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/frozen/impl_unified_A, in the planner's order (PR1, F5, F2 wiring, F3, F1, F4) with amendments A1 to A5, including the starved-GPU rule (A3). Everything sits behind eight env switches, all off by default.

Checked on CPU only: nothing was run on a GPU or a server, so the switches have no end-to-end run or measurement behind them.
- All nine required test files pass on the final code; 76 unit tests were added to five existing files and every pre-existing test passes unmodified (only two import lines grew).
- Switches off: a side-by-side replay against the unchanged prefetcher module (240 random scenarios of 600 events, every mode, read order, timing, gate, hold, soft-pin, price-learning and eviction-policy combination) compared 40,628 log lines of all 17 pre-existing kinds, 48,226 answers and every cache call; all equal.
- Only the prices log on: the same holds apart from its own 26,603 `prices` lines and two fields at the end of `ntp_admit`, so the log switch changes no decision.
- 33 one-line regressions were injected one at a time; each is caught by a new test (the first run missed one, and that test was strengthened).

switches: Common to all eight: typed fields on Envs in environ.py, read once at construction (Switches.read). A switch with nothing to act on in a setup is silently off there (mode observe, no arrival gate, no arrival hold, fifo read order, another read timing); a switch that would act without another switch it needs raises ValueError at construction.

SGLANG_LOG_HICACHE_PRICES_INTERVAL: gates the measuring and one HICACHE_EVT prices line per interval (c, mu, waiting, ready, queued, plans, kappa, late, parked, pend_w, lam, evict_tok, k_us, rec_a_us, rec_b_ns, rec_n, read_ms_page, err_n, err_q10_ms, err_q50_ms, err_q90_ms, rd_lag_ms, q20k, margin_ms, lookup_ms, lag_ms, whold_ms, win_holds, budget_holds, held, write_holds); ntp_admit gains reader= and land_ms= at its end. No decision reads it (checked side by side). Default EnvFloat(0.0) = off. Dependencies: none; works in mode on and observe.

SGLANG_HICACHE_NEXT_TURN_MEASURED_PRICES: priced decisions take measured prices: host room at the eviction frontier's price lam (the hold's quantile; a staged read's rent, where a staging also pays the index of the holder it would evict next), and the harm of a refused read as mu x the fitted prefill cost instead of the constant x queue count. Default EnvBool(False). Acts in mode on only. Dependencies: raises unless --hicache-storage-next-turn-price-learning is off. Turns the measuring on.

SGLANG_HICACHE_NEXT_TURN_FREE_EMPTY_LOOKUPS (F5): the plan's key is cut to what the turn's prompt repeats of it; a lookup that finds nothing gives back what the gate and the queue check charged (at most 8 times a turn) and marks where storage ends, so it is not asked again until the match shrinks below that. New gate answer absent, new line HICACHE_EVT ntp_lookup rid= start= asked= hit= refunded= lookups=. Default EnvBool(False). Acts only in mode on with the arrival gate. Dependencies: none.

SGLANG_HICACHE_NEXT_TURN_LATENESS_WEIGHT (F2): read_start weighs a second of stall by c, the share of admissions that left no ready turn waiting; ec_start gains c= at its end. Default EnvBool(False). Acts only under read timing expected_cost. Dependencies: none; turns the measuring on itself.

SGLANG_HICACHE_NEXT_TURN_READ_LINE (F3): read-time estimates count the parked reads that dispatch orders no later, the rest of a write hold for a timed read, and the read path's measured lags (after 8 samples of each) in place of the seeds. Applies to the staged start, the queue check, the hold, the recompute quotes, and horizon / just-in-time starts while c >= 0.5. ntp_due backlog_pages becomes the line's pages; ec_start gains line_pages= at its end. Default EnvBool(False). Acts only under the deadline read order. Dependencies: raises without LATENESS_WEIGHT when read timing is expected_cost. Turns the measuring on.

SGLANG_HICACHE_NEXT_TURN_HOLD_QUANTILE (F1): a held read starts by minus the q-quantile of the measured admission error at its predicted wait, q = rent / (c + rent) clamped to [0.05, 0.5], instead of the fixed 2 s; the fixed margin stands until that wait's bin holds 30 admissions. ntp_hold gains margin_ms= and q= at its end. Default EnvBool(False). Acts only with the arrival hold. Dependencies: raises without MEASURED_PRICES.

SGLANG_HICACHE_NEXT_TURN_RECOMPUTE_BY_PRICE (F4 with A2): at the gate a turn that arrives with nobody else queued and no ready turn waiting recomputes its missing history when c >= 0.8 and mu_for(recompute_s) x recompute_s < the read's line-aware time; the answer recompute spends no lookup and is priced again at the turn's next call. ntp_gate gains rec_ms= read_ms= mu= c= on priced calls. Default EnvBool(False). Acts only in mode on with the arrival gate. Dependencies: raises without MEASURED_PRICES, READ_LINE (which itself acts only under the deadline read order) or SGLANG_HICACHE_NIXL_SKIP_STORED_WRITES.

SGLANG_HICACHE_NEXT_TURN_RECOMPUTE_WHEN_STARVED (A3): in tick, once the queue has held no ready turn for NTP_GPU_BOUND_S (0.5 s), the first queued turn with a plan and a read still parked gives that read up if recomputing its span is sooner than its landing (new cache method drop_parked_read; a dispatched read is left alone); plan.recompute then makes the gate decline the turn's lookups uncharged. One turn a pass. New line HICACHE_EVT ntp_starve rid= land_ms= rec_ms= tokens= parked=. Default EnvBool(False). Acts only in mode on with the arrival gate. Dependencies: the same three as RECOMPUTE_BY_PRICE.

Why: the two-argument gate, its fixtures and its tests stay as they are, and with the switches off the cache calls exactly what it called before.

Cache attributes: the three new ones (prefetch_gate_prompt_fn, prefetch_lookup_fn, read_lags) are class-level defaults, not set in __init__. Why: the dispatch fixture builds the cache with __new__, and existing tests had to pass unmodified.

Module split: the measuring is a PriceMeter (next_turn_meter.py) and the switch reading a Switches struct (next_turn_switches.py); the plan put both in the prefetcher. Why: the prefetcher would have reached about 2,380 lines. The meter builds the prices line and the prefetcher logs it; PriceBoard.snapshot was not needed.

Ready-turn bookkeeping: the meter keeps its own record; the plan moved the prefetcher's into _follow_ready for everyone. Why: _queue_ahead updates its record only on passes that hold a plan, so one shared record fed every pass changed expected-cost decisions with only the log on. Kept apart, the log changes nothing (checked side by side).

Read-path lags: ReadPathLags lives in next_turn_estimators.py with the write-hold remainder as its method, and the cache feeds it only once the meter installs it; the plan measured always, in cache fields. Why: with every switch off the cache does no new work and keeps no new state.

New log fields are appended only while their switch (or the measuring) is on: ntp_admit reader/land_ms, ec_start c/line_pages, ntp_hold margin_ms/q. The plan appended them always. Why: that changes existing lines with every switch off, against the contract.

Dependencies: a missing switch raises, a structure with nothing to act on makes the switch inert. LATENESS_WEIGHT and READ_LINE turn the measuring on themselves (the plan left LATENESS_WEIGHT silently off without the board). MEASURED_PRICES refuses any price learning. Why: a silently inert switch in a campaign arm is worse than an error, and a learned price would be logged and never used.
mu at saturation is max(light-load value, sessions waiting), not sessions waiting alone (A1). Why: mu must not fall when c crosses 0.1 while few sessions are known to the prefetcher.

lam and the next victim's price are capped at 1e-3, the learned price's ceiling. Why: a victim due within 0.5 s is worth 2 per second, which times the restore cost is far above any price the knob ever took and would stop all staging.

Victims with no holding rate (a queued turn's history, un-hinted prefixes) count as evicted tokens and set no price; the plan dropped them. Why: evict_tok in the prices line would have under-reported eviction.

Late reads and kappa are computed where they are used (the eviction fold, the prices line, the next victim's price), not every pass. Why: nothing reads them in between, and it costs one deadline per parked read.

Admission error: a reader whose landing was not seen is skipped (the plan counted it as a non-reader); a retracted request (negative wait) is skipped here and in the prefill fit; landing times are kept only for planned or queued requests. Why: each of the first two would bias the estimate, and the third keeps that table bounded.
The prices line carries lookup_ms, lag_ms and whold_ms beyond the plan (F3's measured lags; nothing else logs them), beside waiting, plans, queued, ready and the four hold counters (A1, A4).

F5: the gate gets the prompt whole, captured before the cut to a known hit. Why: a retry that knows where the last hit ended cuts the tokens it asks storage for; handed that cut, the gate takes the prompt for one that leaves the key early.
F5: a terminated lookup is not reported to the plan. Why: its hit count of 0 is no answer and would mark history absent and refund wrongly.
F5: RadixKey.match_at gives the shared length; no new common_prefix_len helper. Why: it exists and handles bigram keys.
F5: the free room retry clears lookup_charged. Why: its empty answer must not give back a lookup charged before it.

F2: the plan's guard is built: a staging pays max(frontier price, the next victim's index). A queued turn's history as next victim is priced at the top rate, not as unknown, and the victim is priced at most every 0.5 s. Why: the frontier's price is zero until an eviction happens, so alone it would stage every plan into a full room; pricing costs one priority per evictable host leaf.
F3: two load models, _load on the seeds as today and _line_load on the measured lags, instead of replacing _load. Why: the estimates that leave the line out must keep today's numbers.

F3: horizon and just-in-time starts count the line only while c >= 0.5 (READ_LINE_MIN_C). Why: these timings weigh no cost against an early start, so at saturation the line (42 s at the median in campaign 34) would only pin more history early; the plan's remedy, c through F2, covers expected-cost only.

F3: the line's deadline is the one read_deadline() gives the read, the queue check takes 'now' at the head, and the write hold's remainder is added for timed reads only. Why: the estimate then follows dispatch's own order, and 'now' reads are never write-held.
F3: the fixed lag subtracts the pages completed, not those asked. Why: a read cut for host room completes fewer.

F4: quote_recompute implements A2 and replaces the prototype's recompute_wins. Two more conditions: the lags must be measured, and the missing span is cut to the prompt's tail. Why: on the seeds a recompute wins at every size; and without F5 the key still ends with a reply the prompt does not repeat, which neither a read nor a recompute restores.
